sections.chapter_title: Ethernet (ETH): gigabit media access control (GMAC) with DMA controller
sections.section_title: Performing normal receive and transmit operation
sections.text_helper: Section 76.9.4 "Performing normal receive and transmit operation" in chapter 76 (Ethernet (ETH): gigabit media access control (GMAC) with DMA controller), RM0486 Rev 4, page 4126.
sections.section_content:
For normal operation, complete the following steps:
1. For normal transmit and receive interrupts, read the interrupt status. Then, poll the
descriptor by reading the status of the descriptor owned by the Host (either transmit or
receive).
2. Set the descriptors to appropriate values. Make sure that transmit and receive
descriptors are owned by the DMA to resume the transmission and reception of data.
3. If the descriptors are not owned by the DMA (or no descriptor is available), the DMA
goes into Suspend state. The transmission or reception can be resumed by freeing the
descriptors and writing the ETH_DMAC0TXDTPR (see Channel x Tx descriptor tail
pointer register (ETH_DMACxTXDTPR) and ETH_DMAC0RXDTPR (see Channel x Rx
descriptor tail pointer register (ETH_DMACxRXDTPR)).
4. In debug mode, the values of the current host transmitter or receiver descriptor address
pointer can be read in ETH_DMAC0CATXDR and ETH_DMAC0CARXDR registers
(see Channel x current application transmit descriptor register (ETH_DMACxCATXDR)
and Channel x current application receive descriptor register (ETH_DMACxCARXDR)).
5. In debug mode, the values of the current host transmit buffer address pointer and
receive buffer address pointer can be read in ETH_DMAC0CATXDR and
ETH_DMAC0CARXDR registers (see Channel x current application transmit descriptor
register (ETH_DMACxCATXDR) and Channel x current application receive descriptor
register (ETH_DMACxCARXDR)).
